brief.from: The raw text now sits in one string of 1,115,394 characters, and the script needs to know which distinct characters it contains.

beats.idea: A vocabulary is the set of distinct symbols the model can ever see or emit; at character level it is just the distinct characters in the text.
beats.shows: The learner can say why a model needs a fixed list of symbols before any numbers are assigned.

beats.idea: set(data) walks the 1,115,394-character string and keeps each character once, discarding order and repeats.
beats.shows: Try set('hello') by hand: it gives four items, not five, in no promised order.

beats.idea: sorted(list(set(data))) turns that unordered set into a fixed, repeatable list, so the same text always gives the same character order.
beats.shows: Sort 'hello' to get ['e','h','l','o']; the position of each character in the list is fixed.

beats.idea: len(chars) is the vocabulary size, and the recorded run gives 65, with the printed list starting with newline and space, then punctuation, digits, capitals, lowercase.
beats.shows: Read the comment at lines 64-66 and count the characters to see how 65 is reached.

beats.idea: The sorted order follows character codes, which is why the printed list starts with whitespace and punctuation and puts capitals before lowercase.
beats.shows: Check that 'A' sorts before 'a' and that the printed string matches this order.

brief.to: With the sorted list of 65 characters in hand, the next step is pairing each character with its position, in both directions.
